title: Celebrate City of Forest Day at Green-Wood!
description:
Join Green-Wood’s horticulturists for a morning dedicated to growing a greener, healthier New York City by helping to plant some trees while connecting with with neighbors who care about the future of our urban forest and with the plants that are the future of it! During the event you will not only learn how to plant a tree properly, what a tree needs to thrive, but also discover why trees matter so much to our lives. title: Dinosaurs in Action: Green-Wood’s Birds of Prey
description:
Green-Wood is one of the best places in New York City to spot birds of prey—and not just soaring overhead! Here, you can witness raptors going about their daily lives: hunting and feeding, courting and nesting, learning to fly (a wobbly process!), and simply hanging out.  



Drawing on years of observation and photography, urban naturalist Matthew Wills will take you inside the fascinating world of Green-Wood’s raptors. Through a lively, image-filled presentation, you’ll discover the behaviors and lifestyles of these modern-day heirs of the theropod dinosaurs, from daytime hunters like eagles, hawks, and falcons to the mysterious owls that emerge after dark.

title: Birding In Peace
description:
Before our gates open to the public, this early morning walking tour provides exclusive access to discover the many birds that call Green-Wood home, at least temporarily.  



Stop by this fall and you will see a variety of species passing through. By September, the offspring of summer’s nesting birds will be on their own. title: Grieving & Weaving
description:
Credit: Jordana Bermudez





Join Gelsey Bell at this special edition of Grieving & Weaving. She will present her work that thematically covers the many faces of loss through her vocals and music. 



Stitching together creativity and community, this knitting and crocheting group is unique for one reason: it meets in a cemetery. Whether you’re an expert with yarn or just starting out, you are welcome to join us as we share stories, skills, and grief resources in the comfort of Green-Wood’s Modern Chapel. As we create together, we’ll talk about the significance of handmade items in both our personal and collective histories. To hear about past attendees’ experiences, listen to and/or read this piece featured on NPR.     



Beginners can join our knitting and crochet tutorial groups, while experienced crafters are encouraged to bring ongoing projects and mentor others. Feel free to bring your own yarn, needles, and hooks; some materials will be available on a first-come, first-served basis. Not a knitter? Not to worry, you can bring whatever other crafts you are working on.

title: A Day in the Life of a Funeral Celebrant
description:
Credit: Shannon Taggart





Green-Wood’s A Day in the Life series turns its focus to funeral celebrants, professionals who work closely with families to create meaningful, personalized rituals and memorial services. Panelists will discuss what their day-to-day responsibilities entail, from collaborating with families, funeral directors, and communities to designing services that reflect individual values, cultures, and beliefs. The conversation will also explore the logistics and emotional labor of the role, as well as pathways into the profession. Attendees are invited to ask questions about training, common misconceptions about celebrancy, and the evolving ways people mark death today.

title: Wild Oyster Survey
description:
Wild oysters are a key indicator of ecosystem health in the New York Harbor. Randall’s Island Park Alliance is partnering with the Billion Oyster Project to conduct a wild oyster survey in the Little Hell Gate Salt Marsh.  
Volunteers will have the opportunity to identify oysters and take multiple parameters to determine the abundance, size, and health of the wild oyster population. title: Sake Revolution LIVE! Featuring Austin Power
description:
October 1st is Sake Day — the official start of the sake brewing year in Japan. And every year on the day itself, Sake Revolution, America’s first sake podcast, keeps its favorite tradition: recording a live episode in front of an audience at the Brooklyn Kura Taproom. The kanpai is mandatory… but fun will be inevitable. 
We couldn’t be more excited about this year’s guest: Austin Power (yes, that’s his real name), New York’s most seriously silly sake sommelier and the man behind Accidental Bar, downtown’s beloved neighborhood sake joint on Avenue C. 
A South Carolina kid turned Parsons-trained painter turned sake evangelist, his mission has been, in his own words, “get more people drinking more sake, more irresponsibly” and “if you’re not having fun, you’re doing it wrong”. He honed that philosophy over a decade at legendary NYC sake spots before opening Accidental Bar in 2021. 
Join hosts John and Timothy as they talk to Austin about his take on the sake scene in NYC! 

Come for the party, Leave a little Smarter – we dive into Austin’s philosophy of how to get more people drinking more sake, more irresponsibly and what is the best path forward with the staid and serious world of “Sake Education”
The State of Sake in NYC — real talk on trends, challenges, and bright spots from the sake-selling trenches of NYC – how the NYC sake scene grew from a handful of pioneers into one of the best sake-drinking towns outside Japan.

Fair warning: an evening with Austin is entertainment, full stop. Less lecture, more live show — equal parts tasting, talk show, and party. You’ll laugh, you’ll sip, and somewhere along the way you’ll accidentally learn a lot about sake. 
Your ticket includes a tasting flight hand-picked by Austin himself — Accidental Bar favorites, poured and tasted together during the recording. And bring your questions: we collect written questions from the audience during the show, and our live audience Q&A segment is always a highlight of the episode. 
Come early for happy hour, stay late at the taproom bar, and celebrate Sake Day the only correct way: glass in hand, with friends. Because as Austin says — “If I can see you, aren’t we already friends?!” 
Seats are limited (this one always fills up). Kanpai Ya’ll!

title: Beyond the Classic: Japanese YOUKOKU Relief Ceramics Exhibition by SUIYO @IPPIN Project
description:
Beyond the Classic: Japanese YOUKOKU Relief Ceramics Exhibition by SUIYO @IPPIN Project 
[Introducing the Japanese YOUKOKU Relief Carving Ceramic Collection by Suiyo at IPPIN PROJECT] 
Discover the captivating world of contemporary Japanese ceramics with the YOUKOKU Relief Carving Ceramic Collection by Suiyo, crafted in Aichi, Japan. 
“As we’ve studied the classics, and with an eye on what will remain in the future, we will ‘go beyond’ images, genres, borders, and history, as well as our own past.”
— Daisuke Anayama 
The collection showcases exquisite relief-carved ceramics featuring intricate motifs of auspicious animals, including cranes, turtles, and the animals of the Chinese Zodiac. Each piece brings together traditional Japanese craftsmanship and distinctive sculptural details, creating objects that are both meaningful and beautifully tactile. 
Suiyo’s designs also draw inspiration from the classics of European art. In particular, Suiyo’s painter and carvener, Anayama Fumika’s designs reflects the decorative richness and intricate patterns of Austrian painter Gustav Klimt, creating a fascinating dialogue between Japanese ceramic traditions and European artistic heritage. 
Experience a unique meeting of Eastern and Western cultural influences, where traditional craftsmanship goes beyond borders and is reimagined through a contemporary artistic lens. 
Discover these beautifully crafted pieces at IPPIN PROJECT and bring a touch of Japanese artistry, symbolism, and timeless beauty to your collection. 
*Artist: Daisuke Anayama: a ceramic artist and Fumika Anayama: a painter and carver.
Suiyo is a pottery brand produced by artists, Daisuke Anayama and Fumika Anayama based in Seto, Aichi. The brand concept “Beyond the Classic.” expresses their determination and hope to move forward to make their artworks a new classic in the modern age.

This is the seminal 1984 American concert film featuring a live performance by the American rock band Talking Heads. The film was directed by Jonathan Demme and executive produced by Gary Kurfirst, the band’s longtime manager. The film was shot over four nights in December 1983 at Hollywood’s Pantages Theatre while Talking Heads were on tour promoting their fifth studio album, Speaking in Tongues (1983). Stop Making Sense includes performances of the early Talking Heads single “Psycho Killer” (1977), through to their most recent hit at the time, “Burning Down the House” (1983). It also includes songs from the solo career of frontman David Byrne and by Tom Tom Club, the side project of drummer Chris Frantz and bassist Tina Weymouth. Some have said it’s the greatest band document of all time.

title: Warm Sake Tasting Class and Brewery Tour
description:
Exploring sake temperature and pairing — warm sake, done right, is a revelation. 
For a long time, warm sake has gotten a bad rap! But it can be absolutely delicious when you pick the right sake and the right temperature. Join us for this exciting exploration of sake temperature and the joys of warming sake — the perfect way to explore the subtle umami and richness of premium sake. 
We’ll contrast chilled sake with the same sake served warm, and enjoy carefully selected food pairings to round out the tasting flight. In all, we’ll taste five kinds of sake, each paired with a delicious bite to bring out the flavors and textures. As always, this class includes a behind-the-scenes brewery tour to see how sake is made at NY State’s first sake brewery.
